title: Decide how INV-03 survives portal-only supplier order placement (SL-25)
description:
INV-03 says every state transition in the value chain is writable by an API or an event, never only by a human in a UI. The first real supplier contract surveyed breaks it.

SUP-01's terms, art. 5.3: orders are accepted ONLY through the dealer portal. Telephone and e-mail are refused outright, a placed order cannot be amended, and no API is mentioned anywhere in the document. See SL-05 and SL-25 in 10-architecture/supplier-landscape.md.

This is the single most automation-critical transition in the whole chain - placing the purchase order - and the only surveyed supplier that publishes a dropship contract does not expose it programmatically. The automation charter's readiness test #3 fails against this supplier as contracted.

The choice is load-bearing because it decides how thin the supplier funnel gets. Disqualifying portal-only suppliers may leave no candidate at all in the chosen vertical; admitting them means the charter has an exception surface, which is exactly what docs-ecw is meant to specify.

## Decision
Not yet decided.

## Rationale
To be recorded with the decision.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Disqualify suppliers without an order API. Keeps INV-03 absolute. Cost: may empty the candidate list in fastening and hand tools; unverified whether ANY NL supplier in this vertical publishes an order API.
2. Admit an exception surface, owned and contained per docs-ecw, with the manual step named, bounded and measured. Keeps supply options open. Cost: INV-03 stops being an invariant and becomes a target with exceptions, and the exception is on the highest-volume transition.
3. Treat portal automation as the adapter's problem - the adapter drives the portal rather than an API. Preserves the internal contract in 10-architecture/api-contracts/README.md. Cost: brittle, likely against the supplier's terms, and no supplier contract surveyed permits it.
4. Reclassify INV-03 as an assumption per the derivation question already open in docs-muc. Cheapest on paper, but abandons the property the whole automation thesis rests on.

Do not decide this before docs-sru.1 answers whether a dealer portal exposes an undocumented order API - alternative 1's cost is unknown until then.

title: Obtain feed access from one of the four named NL candidates
description:
Gate on docs-jvy: no feed file was obtained because no supplier account is held. Survey and evidence in 10-architecture/supplier-landscape.md.

Route A was worked on 2026-08-05 and closed off both leads it named. Both suppliers that published a dropship programme in or near this vertical are dead:
- SUP-01 Van Doleweerd / Doleweerd B.V. is bankrupt, trading ceased, site directs questions to the curator. It also turned out to sell scooter parts, never ijzerwaren - the first survey misattributed its vertical.
- SUP-04 gereedschapdropshipping.nl is defunct: no Internet Archive capture since 2022-01-23, TLS certificate expired 2024-10-10 and never renewed, HTTP 403 on every path including plain HTTP.

What remains, in order of expected value:
1. Ask SUP-02 Wovar directly whether it will dropship for a reseller. It has the assortment, the stock, 98% EAN coverage and an ERP behind the shop; it publishes no programme, which is not a refusal. Needs no legal entity to ask.
2. Widen the search beyond dropship-branded suppliers - the wholesale arms of established NL ijzerwaren and gereedschap distributors, and trade directories. Only dropship-branded suppliers were searched, which is how a vertical with real distributors can look empty.
3. SUP-03 Drobbs is live and has a working feed, but only a slice of the vertical. It may still be worth pulling a feed from purely to answer the format and cadence questions in docs-jvy, even if it is never the launch supplier.

Route B, blocked on docs-9fl: registering an account. SUP-03 requires a KvK number, a VAT number and EUR 5.000 minimum annual turnover. Not possible before the operator has a legal entity.

Capture the union of fields, not what the current model asks for - see the REQUIRED section of docs-jvy and the collection rule in CONVENTIONS.md.

Acceptance Criteria: either a sample feed file is in hand, or a supplier has stated in writing what its feed contains and on what cadence; and the outcome of asking SUP-02 is recorded in 10-architecture/supplier-landscape.md
acceptance_criteria: Either a sample feed file is in hand, or a supplier has stated in writing what its feed contains and on what cadence; and the trading status of SUP-01 and the accessibility of SUP-04 are recorded in 10-architecture/supplier-landscape.md

title: Decide whether sourcing is scoped to the order or the order line (AUD-04)
description: Highest late-fix cost in the audit and it has no home. domain-model.md:25 and glossary.md:22 define SourcingDecision per line; all three strategy options at domain-model.md:42 are per-line optimisations and basket consolidation is absent. Verified absences: 'shipping cost', 'freight', 'carriage', 'consolidation' occur zero times in the corpus, and the feed contract sketch names cost/units/currency/lead time but no shipping tariff, free-shipping threshold or per-parcel handling fee. In dropshipping the customer pays one shipping fee and the operator pays one per supplier parcel, so a per-line cheapest-offer rule splits baskets and destroys more margin than the line saving recovers - systematically and invisibly. ADR-0006 already mandates persisting SourcingDecision per order line, so changing this needs an ADR superseding that part, not an edit. NOT covered by docs-2w2, which is transition tables.

But the EPR consequences drawn in market-selection.md HF-05 depend on it, and REG-06 (Authorised Representative for non-established sellers) dates 2026-08-12. HF-05 is currently underivable. Also opens the missing commercial/legal layer: zero occurrences of GDPR, privacy, personal data, legal entity, invoice, KYC in the corpus; one mention of VAT; no PSP decision though iDEAL is called a launch requirement; no DPA though every order sends customer personal data to a supplier.

The premise: attribute-generated copy, in a language the operator does not speak, on the same distributor feeds every competitor has, can win Dutch organic. Second failure mode, from the auditor: the operator cannot assess the quality of that content himself, so the premise can fail SILENTLY - months of output with no internal signal that it is not working. INV-08's second term (CWV/SEO above maintenance and time-to-launch) exists only if the premise holds; ADR-0001, ADR-0002 and ADR-0003 are downstream of that ordering. Blocks the INV-08 half of docs-i6p.

Pull and inspect a real sample feed from a named NL-warehoused distributor. Produces three answers at once: identifier quality (open in ADR-0006), SKU count and cadence and delta-vs-snapshot (inputs to ADR-0005), and evidence the goods are already placed on the EU market (INV-10).

The feed contract sketch omits all of these because the model is per-line (AUD-04), so collecting only what the model requires would confirm the model by construction. docs-dqt cannot be decided without them: whether basket consolidation is possible at all depends on what suppliers publish here.

Per CONVENTIONS, 'a collection task captures the union of what every live option needs'.

Acceptance Criteria: a real feed file from a named NL-warehoused distributor is saved in the repo, with its field list recorded, and the per-parcel tariff, free-shipping threshold, handling fee, whether the supplier consolidates a multi-line PO into one parcel, and any dropship surcharge are recorded alongside it, or noted as absent from the feed
notes:
2026-08-05, desk research done, feed still not obtained. Four candidates named and their published terms recorded in 10-architecture/supplier-landscape.md: SUP-01 Van Doleweerd VOF (dropship contract published, site down), SUP-02 Wovar (best vertical fit, no dropship programme), SUP-03 Drobbs (dropship, partial vertical fit), SUP-04 gereedschapdropshipping.nl (right vertical, blocks automated access).

What the survey already answered, from public sources rather than from a feed:
- parcel economics: EUR 8,50 per Order all-in at SUP-01, EUR 6,95 per order at SUP-03 - both per ORDER, not per line (SL-01, SL-14, SL-23)

What still requires a real feed and is why this issue stays open: cadence, delta versus full snapshot, the actual field list including whether EAN is carried, and SKU count from the feed rather than from a sitemap.

title: Wire the NOISE manifest's reading side into the fixture-run instruction
description:
Parked by operator decision 2026-08-04 - item 3 of the re-review that closed the drift-audit work. Items 1, 2 and 4 were fixed in 75e6ddb; this one was deliberately left, and the fixer was forbidden to touch it.

The producing side is built. `scripts/drift-fixture.py` prints a NOISE manifest naming every class of false positive its own exclusions manufacture, and `40-devops/drift-audit-spec.md:87` states that a reader of a fixture run uses that manifest to tell a fixture artefact from an agent regression.

The reading side is not. `.claude/skills/drift-audit/SKILL.md:53` still says only "compare its findings to the `EXPECT` lines" - nothing tells the reader the manifest exists or what to do with it. So the spec asserts a reader behaviour no instruction produces: the doc-versus-mechanism class this whole system was built to detect, sitting inside the system itself.

What it costs while open: the calibration run is the only check on the auditor after its instructions change. A reader comparing EXPECT lines alone cannot separate a fixture artefact from a real regression, so a regressed auditor can pass calibration.

Remedy: make the fixture-run step compare against both lists - an `EXPECT` line unreported is a regression, a finding matching a NOISE entry is a fixture artefact, anything else is a genuine agent finding. `40-devops/drift-audit-plan.md` is as-planned history and is explicitly not maintained against the files; do not edit it.

title: Require a rule-adding commit to touch docs-check.py or say why it cannot
description:
Measured 2026-08-04: over three days CONVENTIONS went from 8 sections to 11, one new section alone carrying eight distinct rules, while docs-check.py stayed at four checks - all from the original skeleton. That is AUD-07 reproduced by the remediation of AUD-07: the project answered 'you declare constraints and build no instrument' with eight more declarations and no instrument.

The auditor's remedy, and it arrives with its own check unlike the eight: a commit that adds a rule to CONVENTIONS either touches scripts/docs-check.py in the same commit, or states explicitly why the rule is unmechanisable. Enforceable in CI against the diff. Six of the eight rules are judgement and cannot be mechanised - that is fine, but it has to be said so nobody expects them to fire.

title: Decide where agent-instruction authority lives (AUD-13)
description: ADR-0004 makes the docs repo the single source of truth, yet claude-project-instructions.md is a second agent-instruction surface with independent content, no sync mechanism, and demonstrated drift: it names clothing and tableware as vertical examples though market-selection excluded apparel on returns and flagged tableware fragile; it knows nothing of ADR-0007's distributor-only sourcing gate (INV-10, INV-11); it knows nothing of beads and still assumes the docs carry the queue. It is the first context a strategic conversation loads, so it misframes before any doc is read. Options: (a) reduce it to a pointer at INDEX.md so it has nothing to drift with, (b) generate it from the corpus as a session-close step, (c) accept two surfaces and define the sync obligation explicitly. Rejecting the finding is option (c) by default and must be recorded as such. The mechanical half - putting the file under version control - stays in docs-e2h.

title: Add reversibility, appetite and evidence status to the ADR template (AUD-18)
description:
ADR-0006 is the strongest artefact in the repo because it does three things the template never asks for: reasons about reversibility, designs the degenerate case, and states accepted cost concretely. 60-decisions/TEMPLATE.md asks only for Context, Options, Decision, Consequences, Revisit triggers.

Raised from P2 on 2026-08-04. Its only independent defence was that the CONVENTIONS falsifier rule already covers the evidence field - withdrawn by the auditor as false. A rule is an obligation checked at review; a template field is a mechanism that fires while the ADR is being written. That difference is the whole subject of the three-day exchange, so the finding that fixes it cannot be defended by pointing at the rule it exists to mechanise.

Acceptance Criteria: 60-decisions/TEMPLATE.md gains three new fields - reversibility, appetite, evidence status - alongside its existing Context, Options, Decision, Consequences, Revisit triggers

title: Set an appetite and bind scope to solo capacity (AUD-05)
description:
vision.md:37 calls single-operator capacity the binding constraint on every plan, and nothing models against it. roadmap.md:12 cites Shape Up, whose central mechanism is the appetite - fixed time, variable scope - and no appetite is stated for any phase or artefact. Every roadmap exit gate is a quality gate; none is an effort or elapsed-time gate. ADR-0001's revisit trigger, 'solo operation of two runtimes proves unsustainable in Phase 1', has no metric, no threshold and no observer - it will fire as burnout rather than as a measurement.

Live instance, 2026-08-04: audit remediation consumed three days across two sessions and was unplanned scope. It produced a corrected corpus, 31 issues, three new convention sections and six caught contradictions - and verified zero external facts. No feed pulled, no keywords collected, no versions checked. docs-jvy has been 'next' for three days. The remediation was worth doing; the point is that nothing in the plan would have stopped it at three days rather than six.

title: Specify the exception surface - owner, container, contract (AUD-06)
description:
VERIFIED. Readiness-test question 6 requires an escalation path carrying enough context to act on; the charter's north star makes human attention the exception path. c4-context.md:15 has an ADMIN node and that is the only mention - no c4-container row, no runtime, no repo, no owner, no entity in domain-model.md, no state machine, no contract. Failure modes already routed to a human with nowhere to land: unmatched products (VC-03), incomplete content (VC-04), feed quarantine (VC-02), sourcing failure, PO rejection, backorder, partial fulfilment, stale offers, reconciliation drift. Second consequence: until this exists, readiness-test question 6 cannot be answered by any design and the charter's central instrument becomes ceremonial.

Acceptance Criteria: 10-architecture/c4-container.md gains a component for exception handling (owner, runtime, contract) and 10-architecture/domain-model.md gains a matching entity and state machine, so automation-readiness question 6 has a concrete answer for unmatched products, incomplete content, feed quarantine, sourcing failure, PO rejection, backorder, partial fulfilment and stale offers

Prefer the audit's second remedy over the first: do not append VC-20+. VC stages have an owner component, a contract and a state machine; merchandising has no trigger-vs-judgement answer in the same sense and forcing it in dilutes the instrument. State the boundary and name the doc that owns acquisition.

title: Harden docs-check.py to the conventions it claims to enforce
description:
Two of this issue's checks were implemented on 2026-08-04 and are no longer in scope: every INV in the declaration list must carry a derivation (error) and a revisit trigger (warning); every ASM must carry a falsifier, and an incomplete one - no threshold, or 'none exists' - is a warning. Both were verified by injecting a violation and confirming exit 1, then confirming exit 0 after restore. The first version silently caught nothing because the pattern lacked re.M.

REMAINING SCOPE. The orphan check is inert for every ROUTED directory - line 67 passes any file whose parent directory string appears anywhere in INDEX.md, and the routing table names all nine. It DOES fire for a directory absent from INDEX.md entirely.

Design input: three link-check exemptions in two days is a wrong default model, not a growing list. The check assumes every .md under docs/ is a routed living doc; the corpus has at least four classes - living routed, templates, archive, work products - differing in which checks apply, not only in lifetime. A work product legitimately carries forward references to files it proposes creating. Fix is a doc_class field in frontmatter selecting the check set, repairing the orphan check and the link check with one mechanism.

Constraint: doc_class must be the sole authority for check-set selection and must NOT be derivable from status. Encoding the same fact in two fields reproduces AUD-16 inside the new mechanism.

Also unvalidated: paths in related: frontmatter, and markdown [](...) links.

title: Backfill the decision-type sections, then teach WQ-C3 to require them
description:
WQ-C3 does not cover the decision type. REQUIRED_SECTIONS in scripts/queue-check.py keys on task, feature, bug and epic only, so the 12 open decision issues are checked for nothing. Measured 2026-08-05: bd lint reports 12 issues / 32 warnings, all of type decision, all wanting ## Decision, ## Rationale, ## Alternatives Considered. Adding the decision key before the backfill puts CI at 36 errors on the next run, which is why the two halves must land together.

Note the two matchers disagree on form: bd lint wants a '## Name' heading, WQ-C3 wants 'Name:' opening a line. The backfilled text must satisfy both, or WQ-C3's matcher must accept the heading form.

Acceptance Criteria: all 12 open decision issues carry Decision, Rationale and Alternatives Considered; 'decision' is added to REQUIRED_SECTIONS in scripts/queue-check.py in the same commit as the backfill; bd lint reports 0 template warnings and python3 scripts/queue-check.py exits 0.
